events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 17:22:30 and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to the rider, so the fee is only lawful if NS-1 is fully satisfied. [F4 F8] [NS-0 NS-1]

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 17:22:30 and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to the rider, so the fee is only lawful if NS-1 is fully satisfied.

NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here"; the timeline record shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, i.e. the driver never tapped it, while his chat statement claims he did — the system record wins over the statement.

Even taking the driver's own account, he only claimed arrival in chat at 17:19 (chat #1) and cancelled at 17:22:30, and the platform's own arrival record is 17:17:50 with cancellation 4 min 40 s later — the "I'm Here" tap now said to be at 17:18:50 cannot be reconciled with the null tap record in the timeline.
Because at least one of the NS-1 conditions (the required "I'm Here" press) is not met, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The driver's own record shows he sat stationary 53 m from the pickup for 4 min 5 s and could see the rider was coming out a minute after cancellation; there is no traffic, weather or route justification in the records for cancelling rather than completing a Raffles Place → Changi T3 trip.
The driver's statement that the rider was a no-show conflicts with the GPS/timeline record of his own stationary presence and untapped "I'm Here", and chat messages lose to gps/timeline facts.

The driver's account carries 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days out of 3 disputes (394 trips, rating 4.45), which supports asking Ryde to review the account for a repeated pattern of fee-triggering cancellations alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver did stay within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 40 s and his closest approach was 34 m (F2, F3), so NS-1's spatial and waiting-duration prongs (ii) and (iii) are arguably met — only the "I'm Here" prong (i) fails, and if the judge credits the driver's chat claim of pressing the button over the null timeline field, NS-1 would be satisfied and the fee upheld.

The timeline itself records a platform arrival at 17:17:50 and a tap at 17:18:50 with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap (F5, F6), which contradicts the null tap record (F7); a judge could read F6 as proving the tap, weakening C2/C3.

F7 and F6 come from the same timeline source but state opposite things, and the rider's own account that he emerged only after the cancellation (no GPS fact proving the rider was at the pickup within the wait window) means the rider's timeliness is unproven from system records.
No refund can be made in cash and the $6.61 comes back as a non-transferable Ryde voucher (NS-7), which limits the practical value of winning.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: his closest approach to the pickup was 34 m (F1), he first entered the 200 m pickup radius at 17:17:50 (F2/F5), and he then remained stationary 17:18:25–17:22:30 only 53 m from the pickup (F3). This satisfies the 'driver is at the pick-up location according to GPS data' requirement of NS-1 (ii).

The driver waited well beyond the required 3 minutes: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 40 s (F2) and he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after tapping 'I'm Here' (F6), against the ≥ 3:01 threshold in NS-1 (iii).

The rider did not appear within the wait: the driver cancelled at 17:22:30, 6 min 30 s after acceptance and 4 min 40 s after the platform-recorded arrival (F4/F5), i.e. after the full waiting period had elapsed. On these system records the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly charged and no refund is due (NS-1).

The driver's own messages are consistent with the system timeline — he announced his arrival at 17:19 and stated he had waited more than 3 minutes before cancelling at 17:22 (F10/F11), matching the GPS waiting record (F2/F3). Nothing in the chat shows a rider ready and waiting at the kerb.

The rider's account shows 0 no-show disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F16), so there is no pattern of the driver misusing the cancellation button; the rider's 'I came out a minute after' statement is unsupported by any timeline fact and must yield to the GPS/timeline records that show the driver on station for over 4 minutes (F2/F3/F5).

In the alternative, even if the '$6.61 stands' finding were not made, NS-2's aggravated consequence does not apply here: the driver's GPS shows him within 200 m of the pickup when he cancelled (F2/F3), so there is no false 'I'm Here'/not-at-pickup combination that would support an account flag under NS-2.

weaknesses: The timeline facts F6 and F7 contradict each other on whether the driver tapped 'I'm Here' (F6 gives 17:18:50 at 38 m; F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null). NS-1 (i) requires the tap, so the rider will argue the first condition fails — my case rests on the GPS/timeline waiting record (F2/F3/F5) rather than on the disputed tap.
The driver's written statement (F12) and chat (F10/F11) are self-serving and, under the system-records-win rule, cannot carry the finding; they only corroborate the GPS timing.

The driver has 3 disputes with 2 no-show findings upheld in 90 days (F17), which the rider can use to argue a pattern of no-show cancellations and to invite a flag_account request under NS-2 / RD-6 logic, even though the record here shows the driver was physically at the pickup (F1/F2/F3).

The rider's account is long-standing with a clean dispute record (F16), which may incline the judge toward accepting the rider's 'I came out a minute later' account despite the absence of any timeline fact supporting it.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 6 points
events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Concede the spatial prong: the driver's closest approach was 34 m (F1) and he sat stationary 53 m from the pickup (F3), so NS-1 (ii) is met — but NS-1 requires (i), (ii) AND (iii) cumulatively ("同时满足"), and D1 says nothing about the tap. [F1 F3] [NS-1]
→ D2: The waiting-duration prong is not decisive either way: D2's own best fact (F6) is the very field the timeline contradictorily reports as null (F7), so a finding built on F6 cannot rescue NS-1 (iii) without first proving the tap that F6 assumes. [F6 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D3: D3 asks the judge to infer a lawful no-show fee from elapsed time alone, but NS-1 is conjunctive and the required "I'm Here" press is recorded as never made (F7), so the $6.61 charged per F8 must be refunded in full under NS-2. [F7 F8 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: D4 is built entirely on the driver's own messages and statement (F10, F11, F12), which under the system-records-win rule cannot carry NS-1 (i) when the timeline record of the tap is null (F7); note also that the driver only announced he was "here" at 17:19 (F10) while claiming to have tapped at 17:18:50 (F6). [F10 F11 F12 F7 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D5: F16 is a profile fact about the rider and, per the rules, can never decide the main finding — the rider's non-appearance is not what is in dispute; the fee's validity turns on the driver's tap record (F7), not on the rider's history. [F16 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D6: No flag_account is requested on a false "I'm Here" ground, so D6 is moot; F17 still legitimately supports sending the driver's account for review as a repeated no-show-fee pattern (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d), which is an additional action only and not the basis of the finding. [F17] [NS-2 RD-6]
Revised ask: refund_full $6.61

The waiting-duration prong is not decisive either way: D2's own best fact (F6) is the very field the timeline contradictorily reports as null (F7), so a finding built on F6 cannot rescue NS-1 (iii) without first proving the tap that F6 assumes.

D3 asks the judge to infer a lawful no-show fee from elapsed time alone, but NS-1 is conjunctive and the required "I'm Here" press is recorded as never made (F7), so the $6.61 charged per F8 must be refunded in full under NS-2.

D4 is built entirely on the driver's own messages and statement (F10, F11, F12), which under the system-records-win rule cannot carry NS-1 (i) when the timeline record of the tap is null (F7); note also that the driver only announced he was "here" at 17:19 (F10) while claiming to have tapped at 17:18:50 (F6).

F16 is a profile fact about the rider and, per the rules, can never decide the main finding — the rider's non-appearance is not what is in dispute; the fee's validity turns on the driver's tap record (F7), not on the rider's history.

No flag_account is requested on a false "I'm Here" ground, so D6 is moot; F17 still legitimately supports sending the driver's account for review as a repeated no-show-fee pattern (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d), which is an additional action only and not the basis of the finding.

events.body:

[F3 F13 F14 F15] [NS-1 NS-3]
→ C6: The statement is not the basis of the finding: the driver's GPS shows him at the pickup for over four minutes (F1/F2/F3), and the chat merely corroborates that timing (F10/F11); the rider's uncorroborated 'came out a minute later' account has no supporting gps or timeline fact at all. [F1 F2 F3 F10 F11] [NS-1]
→ C7: A profile fact cannot decide the case and here it cuts the other way on severity: the driver's approach to the pickup is 34 m and his wait well exceeds the 3-minute trigger (F1/F2/F6), so there is no false 'I'm Here' or not-at-pickup combination of the kind NS-2 flags. [F17 F1 F2 F6] [NS-2]

points.response: Conceded as a framing point only: the fee's lawfulness turns on NS-1, and on the system records it is satisfied — driver closest approach 34 m (F1), inside 200 m from 17:17:50 (F2/F5), stationary 53 m away 17:18:25–17:22:30 (F3).

This reads the tap requirement as a binary that ignores F6, which records the tap at 17:18:50, 38 m from pickup, with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m afterwards; where F7 and F6 conflict within the same timeline source, NS-1's substantive test — GPS presence at the pickup plus more than 3 minutes waited — is met on F1/F2/F3 regardless.

There is no irreconcilable conflict: F6 supplies a concrete tap time of 17:18:50, 60 s after the platform arrival record at 17:17:50 (F5), and the driver's chat at 17:19 (F10) simply restates that he was on site — the 34 m closest approach (F1) and the stationary spell 53 m from pickup (F3) place him at the point the chat claims.

NS-2's refund only follows if a condition of NS-1 fails, and the GPS and timeline records show conditions (ii) and (iii) satisfied — 4 min 40 s cumulative inside 200 m and 3 min 40 s after the recorded tap (F2/F6) — so the $6.61 charge stands.

That the driver was stationary near the pickup is precisely what NS-1 (ii) requires (F3), and nothing in the records shows the rider presented himself at the pickup within the wait window; the absence of traffic or route justification (F13/F14/F15) is irrelevant once the no-show conditions are met, since NS-3 concerns cancellations where no-show is not established.

The statement is not the basis of the finding: the driver's GPS shows him at the pickup for over four minutes (F1/F2/F3), and the chat merely corroborates that timing (F10/F11); the rider's uncorroborated 'came out a minute later' account has no supporting gps or timeline fact at all.

A profile fact cannot decide the case and here it cuts the other way on severity: the driver's approach to the pickup is 34 m and his wait well exceeds the 3-minute trigger (F1/F2/F6), so there is no false 'I'm Here' or not-at-pickup combination of the kind NS-2 flags.
I withdraw D6 as unnecessary: the flag question is the judge's to raise, and my case rests on NS-1 being satisfied by F1/F2/F3/F6.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the driver, so the only route by which the $6.61 can stand is NS-1, which requires the three conditions of arrival confirmation, GPS presence at the pickup and more than three minutes of waiting to be satisfied cumulatively [F4][F8][NS-0][NS-1]. The rider's complaint that he "came out a minute after" the cancellation is an unsupported statement: no gps or timeline fact shows the rider at the pickup within the wait window, and system records take precedence over statements [F2][F3][F4][NS-1].

On the three NS-1 conditions: the platform arrival indicator (F6) records the driver tapping "I'm Here" at 17:18:50, which satisfies condition (i) [F6][NS-1]. Condition (ii) is settled and conceded by the rider: the driver was 38 m from the pickup at the moment of the tap and his closest approach was 34 m, inside the pickup radius [F1][F6][NS-1]. Condition (iii) is likewise settled: after the tap he remained inside the radius for 3 min 40 s (220 s > 180 s), and cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 40 s [F2][F6][NS-1].

The driver's arrival and waiting are independently corroborated by the timeline: accepted 17:16:00, platform arrival recorded 17:17:50, cancelled by driver at 17:22:30 — 6 min 30 s after acceptance and 4 min 40 s after arrival [F4][F5][NS-1]. His stationary spell of 4 min 5 s only 53 m from the pickup, and the absence of any traffic incidents or speed-band records on the route, are consistent with a genuine wait for a rider who did not appear [F3][F13][F14][NS-1].

The rider's case turns on F7 (driver_pressed_here_at null) contradicting F6. Both records come from the same timeline source, and F6 is the concrete arrival-confirmation entry on which the execution trace relies; it is corroborated by the driver's chat ("I'm here at the pickup point") and the pre-cancellation message that he had waited more than 3 minutes, and by the independent GPS presence [F6][F10][F11][F1][F2][F3][NS-1]. claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 17:22:30 and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to the rider, so the fee is only lawful if NS-1 is fully satisfied.

NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed "I'm Here"; the timeline record shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, i.e. the driver never tapped it, while his chat statement claims he did — the system record wins over the statement.

Even taking the driver's own account, he only claimed arrival in chat at 17:19 (chat #1) and cancelled at 17:22:30, and the platform's own arrival record is 17:17:50 with cancellation 4 min 40 s later — the "I'm Here" tap now said to be at 17:18:50 cannot be reconciled with the null tap record in the timeline.
Because at least one of the NS-1 conditions (the required "I'm Here" press) is not met, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full under NS-2.

The driver's own record shows he sat stationary 53 m from the pickup for 4 min 5 s and could see the rider was coming out a minute after cancellation; there is no traffic, weather or route justification in the records for cancelling rather than completing a Raffles Place → Changi T3 trip.
The driver's statement that the rider was a no-show conflicts with the GPS/timeline record of his own stationary presence and untapped "I'm Here", and chat messages lose to gps/timeline facts.

The driver's account carries 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days out of 3 disputes (394 trips, rating 4.45), which supports asking Ryde to review the account for a repeated pattern of fee-triggering cancellations alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver did stay within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 40 s and his closest approach was 34 m (F2, F3), so NS-1's spatial and waiting-duration prongs (ii) and (iii) are arguably met — only the "I'm Here" prong (i) fails, and if the judge credits the driver's chat claim of pressing the button over the null timeline field, NS-1 would be satisfied and the fee upheld.

The timeline itself records a platform arrival at 17:17:50 and a tap at 17:18:50 with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after the tap (F5, F6), which contradicts the null tap record (F7); a judge could read F6 as proving the tap, weakening C2/C3.

F7 and F6 come from the same timeline source but state opposite things, and the rider's own account that he emerged only after the cancellation (no GPS fact proving the rider was at the pickup within the wait window) means the rider's timeliness is unproven from system records.
No refund can be made in cash and the $6.61 comes back as a non-transferable Ryde voucher (NS-7), which limits the practical value of winning.

claims.assertion: The driver was physically at the pickup point: his closest approach to the pickup was 34 m (F1), he first entered the 200 m pickup radius at 17:17:50 (F2/F5), and he then remained stationary 17:18:25–17:22:30 only 53 m from the pickup (F3). This satisfies the 'driver is at the pick-up location according to GPS data' requirement of NS-1 (ii).

The driver waited well beyond the required 3 minutes: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 40 s (F2) and he stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after tapping 'I'm Here' (F6), against the ≥ 3:01 threshold in NS-1 (iii).

The rider did not appear within the wait: the driver cancelled at 17:22:30, 6 min 30 s after acceptance and 4 min 40 s after the platform-recorded arrival (F4/F5), i.e. after the full waiting period had elapsed. On these system records the $6.61 cancellation fee is properly charged and no refund is due (NS-1).

The driver's own messages are consistent with the system timeline — he announced his arrival at 17:19 and stated he had waited more than 3 minutes before cancelling at 17:22 (F10/F11), matching the GPS waiting record (F2/F3). Nothing in the chat shows a rider ready and waiting at the kerb.

The rider's account shows 0 no-show disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F16), so there is no pattern of the driver misusing the cancellation button; the rider's 'I came out a minute after' statement is unsupported by any timeline fact and must yield to the GPS/timeline records that show the driver on station for over 4 minutes (F2/F3/F5).

In the alternative, even if the '$6.61 stands' finding were not made, NS-2's aggravated consequence does not apply here: the driver's GPS shows him within 200 m of the pickup when he cancelled (F2/F3), so there is no false 'I'm Here'/not-at-pickup combination that would support an account flag under NS-2.

weaknesses: The timeline facts F6 and F7 contradict each other on whether the driver tapped 'I'm Here' (F6 gives 17:18:50 at 38 m; F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null). NS-1 (i) requires the tap, so the rider will argue the first condition fails — my case rests on the GPS/timeline waiting record (F2/F3/F5) rather than on the disputed tap.
The driver's written statement (F12) and chat (F10/F11) are self-serving and, under the system-records-win rule, cannot carry the finding; they only corroborate the GPS timing.

The driver has 3 disputes with 2 no-show findings upheld in 90 days (F17), which the rider can use to argue a pattern of no-show cancellations and to invite a flag_account request under NS-2 / RD-6 logic, even though the record here shows the driver was physically at the pickup (F1/F2/F3).

The rider's account is long-standing with a clean dispute record (F16), which may incline the judge toward accepting the rider's 'I came out a minute later' account despite the absence of any timeline fact supporting it.

points.response: Concede the spatial prong: the driver's closest approach was 34 m (F1) and he sat stationary 53 m from the pickup (F3), so NS-1 (ii) is met — but NS-1 requires (i), (ii) AND (iii) cumulatively ("同时满足"), and D1 says nothing about the tap.

The waiting-duration prong is not decisive either way: D2's own best fact (F6) is the very field the timeline contradictorily reports as null (F7), so a finding built on F6 cannot rescue NS-1 (iii) without first proving the tap that F6 assumes.

D3 asks the judge to infer a lawful no-show fee from elapsed time alone, but NS-1 is conjunctive and the required "I'm Here" press is recorded as never made (F7), so the $6.61 charged per F8 must be refunded in full under NS-2.

D4 is built entirely on the driver's own messages and statement (F10, F11, F12), which under the system-records-win rule cannot carry NS-1 (i) when the timeline record of the tap is null (F7); note also that the driver only announced he was "here" at 17:19 (F10) while claiming to have tapped at 17:18:50 (F6).

F16 is a profile fact about the rider and, per the rules, can never decide the main finding — the rider's non-appearance is not what is in dispute; the fee's validity turns on the driver's tap record (F7), not on the rider's history.

No flag_account is requested on a false "I'm Here" ground, so D6 is moot; F17 still legitimately supports sending the driver's account for review as a repeated no-show-fee pattern (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d), which is an additional action only and not the basis of the finding.

Conceded as a framing point only: the fee's lawfulness turns on NS-1, and on the system records it is satisfied — driver closest approach 34 m (F1), inside 200 m from 17:17:50 (F2/F5), stationary 53 m away 17:18:25–17:22:30 (F3).

This reads the tap requirement as a binary that ignores F6, which records the tap at 17:18:50, 38 m from pickup, with 3 min 40 s inside 200 m afterwards; where F7 and F6 conflict within the same timeline source, NS-1's substantive test — GPS presence at the pickup plus more than 3 minutes waited — is met on F1/F2/F3 regardless.

There is no irreconcilable conflict: F6 supplies a concrete tap time of 17:18:50, 60 s after the platform arrival record at 17:17:50 (F5), and the driver's chat at 17:19 (F10) simply restates that he was on site — the 34 m closest approach (F1) and the stationary spell 53 m from pickup (F3) place him at the point the chat claims.

NS-2's refund only follows if a condition of NS-1 fails, and the GPS and timeline records show conditions (ii) and (iii) satisfied — 4 min 40 s cumulative inside 200 m and 3 min 40 s after the recorded tap (F2/F6) — so the $6.61 charge stands.

That the driver was stationary near the pickup is precisely what NS-1 (ii) requires (F3), and nothing in the records shows the rider presented himself at the pickup within the wait window; the absence of traffic or route justification (F13/F14/F15) is irrelevant once the no-show conditions are met, since NS-3 concerns cancellations where no-show is not established.

The statement is not the basis of the finding: the driver's GPS shows him at the pickup for over four minutes (F1/F2/F3), and the chat merely corroborates that timing (F10/F11); the rider's uncorroborated 'came out a minute later' account has no supporting gps or timeline fact at all.

A profile fact cannot decide the case and here it cuts the other way on severity: the driver's approach to the pickup is 34 m and his wait well exceeds the 3-minute trigger (F1/F2/F6), so there is no false 'I'm Here' or not-at-pickup combination of the kind NS-2 flags.
I withdraw D6 as unnecessary: the flag question is the judge's to raise, and my case rests on NS-1 being satisfied by F1/F2/F3/F6.
